overview: One block: a copper tap. Hang it under a block or fix it to a wall, and it pours a whole source block of whatever water or lava sits on the far side of that block.
Water is endless, as it is from dripstone. Lava is not: every pour empties the lava it came from.

1.0.0: The copper spigot, from three copper ingots in a hook.
Hangs from the underside of a block, or juts from the side of one with its spout turned down. Never on a floor.
Draws from the block beyond its support: a water or lava source, a waterlogged block, or a full cauldron.
Pours into the cauldron beneath it, filling it to the brim, or puts a source block down wherever a bucket could.
Turns on a right-click, or once each time a redstone signal arrives.
Lava poured is lava gone from the source. Water boils off in the Nether, as a bucket's does.
